images.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Project asset Aleria: the venerable trading post of Markt der Fortuna in medieval Gwynthor, a rival to Klingende Münze, historically rooted here for centuries. Vertical 2:3 image. Tales of Xillia/Frieren Anime Art Style. Clear anime lineart and clean cel shading, soft simple stone, cloth and timber textures. No realistic textures, no photorealism, no painterly rendering. A broad old harbor courtyard enclosed by prosperous medieval pale-stone and timber counting houses with rounded arcades, weathered but meticulously maintained, green shutters, cream and forest-green hangings bearing a small simplified classical columned pavilion motif. In one wing a blue-decorated bank entrance, along the waterfront rows of timber warehouses and a shipyard working on a broad-bellied MERCHANT vessel with open cargo hatches, no warship. The main impression is an established merchant community, guild masters, long-used cobbles and generations of trade, not a newly built palace. A few small human merchants and dock hands, rounded human ears, mostly brown or red hair at a distance. Daylight, harbor masts and the medieval city on a rise in background. Calm readable composition from the courtyard entrance, a little lower and more intimate than an aerial view, tall architecture. No legible lettering, no modern machinery, no coins or red-company symbols, no modern marketplace stalls clutter, no royal throne or flags of real countries.

Use case: illustration-story. Aleria project asset: the council chamber of Markt der Fortuna in Gwynthor. Vertical 2:3. Tales of Xillia/Frieren anime art style, clear anime lineart and clean cel shading, soft simple materials, no photorealism, no painterly rendering. A venerable medieval merchant council room, broad round oak table with nine equal unoccupied chairs around it, same height and upholstery, no throne or head chair. Soft forest-green and cream hangings, one small classical columned pavilion ornament above an arched doorway, no invented family heraldry. Tall open arched windows face the old harbor and trading sails. A few closed ledger books, small cloth-bound sample bundles, one cooper's barrel miniature and rolled sea charts on the table express trade and craft, keep the tabletop mostly clear. The room feels maintained through centuries of daily use, wood polished by generations, white stone and timber beams, calm afternoon daylight. Wide enough framing to see all seats and the table comfortably, generous empty floor foreground. No people, no readable text, no modern furniture, no royal decorations, no red-company symbolism.

Three solid oak cashier desks with restrained brass weighing scales, closed ledgers, small coin trays, behind them iron lattice and a locked strongroom door. Open foreground waiting area, a second smaller desk near the window for merchant letters. Emphasis on generations of banking and maritime commerce, not modern luxury. Empty of people, no lettering, no red or golden lion motif, no modern safe dial, no computers, banknotes, clocks or modern furniture. Composition simple and spacious.
